Joking about people dying in Palestine just to call BTS Zionist is not funny. Real human suffering—children, families, entire neighborhoods—should never be reduced to a punchline or a meme for online fandom arguments. Whether someone is mocking the accusation or leaning into it, treating the death toll as comedy material is tasteless and shows a complete lack of basic empathy for people living through it. As for the numbers (as of early September 2026): Gaza According to the Gaza Ministry of Health (the primary source used by the UN, WHO, and most international agencies), roughly 73,600–73,650 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since October 7, 2023, with about 174,500–174,600 injured. These figures include both civilians and combatants; the ministry does not break them down that way. A U.S.-brokered ceasefire took effect around October 10–11, 2025. Since then, the same health authorities report more than 1,300 additional deaths and over 4,400 injuries from continued Israeli strikes and operations, despite the formal truce. Children specifically •  A June 2026 UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry report found that at least 20,179 children were killed in Gaza between October 7, 2023 and October 7, 2025 (about 30% of the total death toll at that point). This included over 5,000 children under age 5 and hundreds of newborns. •  UNICEF and other agencies have reported roughly 300 more children killed in the roughly 300 days after the ceasefire began (an average of about one child per day). •  Broader UNICEF tracking puts the total of children killed or injured since October 2023 above 64,000. Save the Children has cited at least 21,000 children confirmed killed by around the 1,000-day mark of the war. Thousands more are believed still buried under rubble and not yet counted. West Bank (including East Jerusalem) UN OCHA data shows more than 1,100 Palestinians killed since October 2023, including at least 240 children. Israeli side for context On October 7, 2023, Hamas and other groups killed about 1,200 people in Israel (mostly civilians, including roughly 40 children) and took 251 hostages. Israeli military and other fatalities since then bring the overall Israeli death toll to roughly 2,200–2,240. These numbers come primarily from the Gaza Ministry of Health, cross-checked and regularly cited by UN agencies (OCHA, UNRWA, UNICEF, WHO). Independent analyses and even some Israeli officials have described the overall scale as broadly accurate, though debates continue over exact civilian-vs-combatant ratios, undercounting of bodies still under rubble, and indirect deaths from disease, starvation, and lack of medical care. The true human cost is almost certainly higher than the confirmed figures. None of this is abstract or meme material. These are real people.
